title: Contact holdouts gave positive prediction skill under random input labels in one leech circuit
abstract: We tested two validation rules for a spatial activity predictor in one matched leech circuit. The main sample had 271 contacts from 35 mapped inputs to motor neuron DE-3R. Each input activity value was copied to all its contacts. At a 20 micrometre path scale, the exact mean skill under random input labels was 0.328 for a contact holdout and -0.270 for a whole-input holdout. Observed contact skills were 0.290 in swim and 0.295 in left bend, below their random-label means. We derived an exact finite-label risk identity and checked it by exhaustive synthetic permutations, 9999 data label draws, and direct prediction calculations. Positive contact-level skill can therefore occur without a location rule that predicts new inputs. The result audits defined methods, not the source authors. One animal, uncertain matches, copied soma labels, and absent raw trace errors limit biological inference. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes, and external retrieval instructions support reproduction. Source records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Contact and input holdouts differ under random input labels in the fixed 35-input circuit. Exact means and observed skills use the same baseline. Label ranges are not animal confidence intervals.
